newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe details subscriber costs plan.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe details subscriber costs plan.

text.p: CompuServe Corp Chief Financial Officer Lawrence Gyenes said the company's method of accounting for subscriber costs was being accelerated to reflect how long typical subscribers remain with its service.
But the move stopped short of entirely doing away with the practice of deferring customer acquisition costs.
Gyenes said accounting for such costs will continue to run over a 24-month period, as the company has traditionally done, but that the rate of amortization would be accelerated.
CompuServe's plan to clean up its accounting practices follows a similar move by America Online Inc.

Although once an accepted practice within the industry, which borrowed the practice from the nascent cable TV industry, Wall Street analysts had long criticized the measure as a means of artificially inflating quarterly earnings.

Instead of spreading such expenses over two years, Gyenes said the company now plans to expense 50 percent of such marketing costs in the quarter in which they are incurred, and another 30 percent over the following nine months.
In effect, it would expense 80 percent of such costs in the first year. The remaining 20 percent would be accounted for over the course of the second year, he said.
